subject.title: fix(gateway): prevent cross-client system-agent session takeover

question: For device-less loopback token/password CLI calls, should system-agent ownership remain connection-scoped with the client workflow reusing one socket, or is there a server-verifiable per-caller identity that can safely survive reconnects?
rationale: A shared credential cannot safely become a caller identity without collapsing distinct clients back into the takeover condition; choosing the durable identity or connection-lifecycle contract is a security and product-boundary decision.

options.title: Reuse one gateway connection for the conversation
options.body: Keep the new connection-scoped fail-closed ownership rule and update the affected CLI/onboarding workflow to send its system-agent turns over one live connection.

options.title: Define a verified reconnect identity
options.body: Introduce a server-verifiable per-caller identity only if it distinguishes clients sharing the same token/password and is documented and tested across reconnects.

recommendation.title: Reuse one gateway connection for the conversation
recommendation.body: Keep the new connection-scoped fail-closed ownership rule and update the affected CLI/onboarding workflow to send its system-agent turns over one live connection.

likelyOwner.reason: The unresolved decision is within the gateway session-ownership implementation introduced by these commits.
